summary: The narrator, Russell, has killed seven attackers in a hallway and returns to a room with Arthur, who holds a Beretta. Russell stops watching the door, pretends to repair a PCI card by prying off microchips, and keeps his eyes on the circuit board as Rio instructed. A single set of footsteps enters, and Dawna Polk speaks, saying the narrator has something she needs and that she won't kill him. The passage ends with her observing him from close behind.
one_line: In a tense fiction excerpt from Book 2, Russell fakes repairing a circuit board as the villain Dawna Polk enters and confronts him.
key_facts: The narrator had taken out the remaining seven attackers in the hallway before returning to the doorway.
The narrator handed Arthur a share of the new munitions taken from the downed enemies.
Arthur held a Beretta at high ready while watching the blood-covered hall.
The narrator had a stolen M4 settled against his shoulder while waiting in the doorway.
The narrator said 'We fight' when Arthur asked about the plan, and replied 'Can't fight forever' to Arthur's objection.
Arthur mumbled, 'God help me, I maybe believe you,' so softly he may not have known he said it aloud.
The narrator picked up a PCI card and began prying tiny microchips off it with a utility knife, though he did not know what it did.
The narrator kept his eyes on the circuit board in his hand, as Rio had told him to do.
Rio had also cautioned the narrator not to speak.
Only one set of footsteps entered the hallway, one light, quiet set.
Dawna Polk entered the room and said, 'Good evening.'
Dawna Polk said, 'You have something I need,' and 'You won't kill me.'
Dawna Polk said she was unusually effective at dispatching her people and would hate to be caught in a crossfire.
The narrator's hand was shaking from gripping the utility knife, and he was fairly sure he felt terror.
The passage ends with Dawna Polk's eyes piercing the narrator's neck from behind as she observed him.
